rounds.text: Bafna Pharmaceuticals is currently trading at a significant premium, with a P/E ratio of 52x to 57.1x, far exceeding the sector benchmark of 30.67x [E1, E6]. This valuation is further strained by a price-to-book ratio of 6.01x, while a discounted cash flow analysis suggests an intrinsic value of only Rs 142 per share, resulting in a negative margin of safety of 72.2% [E2, E45, E46]. The market price, sitting at 98% of its 52-week range, appears to bake in an aggressive 21.5% earnings growth expectation, which is substantially higher than the 14.0% base case assumption [E5, E47]. Furthermore, the company’s long-term performance is concerning, evidenced by a 10-year median return on equity of -6% and a dismal return on assets of -45.61% compared to the sector benchmark of 5.69% [E8, E26]. Investors are also receiving no compensation for these risks, as the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: [E11, E13, E27, E28, E29, E56].
